q: If $v$ is a number, what do you know about $v^2$'s prime factors in $x(x+1)=v^2$? Can $x$ and $x+1$ have any of the same factors? Do their prime factors come in pairs, so that this means they are square numbers as well? What about $x(x+1)=v^3$ and $x(x+1)=v^n$?
answer: $x$ and $x+1$ share no prime factors, so the prime factors of $v^2$ must split into pairs that each belong wholly to $x$ or to $x+1$. This means $x$ and $x+1$ are both square numbers. So $x(x+1)=v^2$ has no solutions, since there are no two consecutive square numbers.
